about.p1: I embraced computer science for the sense of freedom it gives. The freedom to act, to create, to change and, when possible, to innovate.
about.p2: I graduated from Sapienza University of Rome, completing both my bachelor's and master's degrees with top marks. I am a dynamic person, sometimes contradictory, constantly evolving. I never stand still: my creative restlessness and the drive to challenge myself and push my limits are what keep me working for hours on a project I consider “mine.”
about.p3: After years of working while studying and gaining professional experience in different companies, I decided to give myself a different opportunity: to build something truly my own. I founded a startup, putting my experience, years of study and personal sacrifices at the service of my own ideas and vision. I design software architectures and develop full-stack solutions, integrating AI systems built to solve real-world problems.
about.p4: I am a positive, curious and meticulous person. I constantly question myself. I am always looking for new paths to explore, new ways to grow, and new projects worth dedicating myself to.

header.quote: "For the roads, they go on without end."

about.p1: Since the dawn of time, humanity has lived in God's shadow, seeking Him and envying His greatest privilege: the capacity to create. Condemned to finitude, man invented art to emulate that miracle, shaping stories and figures to feel like the master of a destiny.
about.p2: However, only computer science allows us to transcend the stasis of the canvas. Programming is the ultimate creative act, where logic becomes matter and thought becomes action. The thirst for omnipotence is quenched in every algorithm that works, in every system that springs to life beneath our fingers. If art imitates life, computer science simulates it. And in that microcosm of rules and variables, man finally touches the divine illusion of having created life itself.
about.p3: Perhaps one day the spell will break, for I have realized that giving life to one’s own creatures consumes the soul. Yet, it is a destiny I cannot evade. Every morning, facing the glow of the screen, I listen to that whisper which overpowers all reason: it is not a choice, it is a necessity. I must continue playing God until the voice of sleep screams louder than the voice of programming.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: Yes. All core features — notes, tasks, events, reminders — work fully offline. Your data lives on your device.
faq.q2: Do I need to create an account?
faq.a2: No account, no email, no password. Open the app and start capturing immediately.
faq.a3: Local-first means your data is stored on your device and works without a server. You own it, you control it, and it is available even when offline.
faq.q4: Is my data synced to the cloud?
faq.a4: Core capture and planning flows are fully on-device. Optional sync is on the roadmap but never required.
faq.q5: Can I export my notes and tasks?
faq.a5: Yes. Your data is not locked in. Export options are available so you are never stuck.
faq.a6: Anyone who wants a fast, private, distraction-free way to capture notes and tasks without the overhead of complex productivity suites.
faq.q7: How is Capture different from team workspace apps?
faq.a7: Capture is built for personal quick capture and daily focus. It avoids shared-workspace complexity, permissions setup, and heavy project structure.
faq.q8: Can I use Capture as a minimalist to-do app?
faq.a8: Yes. Capture includes tasks, scheduling, and reminders, but keeps the workflow lightweight so you can focus on one clear next action.

CapturePrivacy.title: Capture Privacy Policy
CapturePrivacy.subtitle: This page explains what data Capture uses and how it is handled. Capture is designed to work locally on your device without account-based cloud storage.

audience.title: Audience and Scope
audience.body: Capture is intended for users aged 13 and above. The app is not directed to children under 13 years of age.

data.title: Data We Process
data.body: Capture stores user-created content such as notes, tasks, events, tags, links, timing fields, language and reminder preferences, and optional photo attachments. This information is stored locally on your device.

usage.title: How We Use Data
usage.body: Data is used to power core app features such as capture, planning views, calendar scheduling, and local reminders.

sharing.title: Data Sharing
sharing.body: Capture does not require user accounts and does not upload your notes, tasks, events, or photos to a backend service. We do not sell personal data.

retention.title: Retention and Deletion
retention.body: Your data remains on your device until you delete it in the app, clear app storage, or uninstall the app.

rights.title: User Rights
rights.body: You can modify or delete your content directly in the app. For privacy questions or clarifications, you can contact us at the address below.

children.title: Children's Privacy
children.body: Because Capture targets users 13+, we do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13. If such data is identified, it is removed promptly.

changes.title: Policy Updates
changes.body: We may update this policy over time. Material changes are reflected on this page with an updated effective date.

PyQuark.tagline: Dual-protocol install server with virtualized archives
PyQuark.description: PyQuark is a Python-based remote file server for Nintendo Switch installers. It auto-detects Goldleaf or DBI clients and adapts transport behavior so you can install NSP/XCI content directly, including from compressed archives.

protocols.label: Protocol Modes
protocols.goldleaf: Quark-compatible workflow with on-the-fly XCI virtualization into installable NSP structures.
protocols.dbi: Native DBI0 streaming path for robust high-speed installs, especially recommended for XCI dumps.

dual.title: Dual Client Support
dual.desc: Automatically switches between Goldleaf Quark protocol and DBI0 flow based on the connected homebrew client.

xci.title: XCI Smart Handling
xci.desc: Supports virtual XCI-to-NSP mapping for Goldleaf and native XCI streaming for DBI without manual conversion.

rar.title: Archive-Native Access
rar.desc: Reads single and multi-part RAR archives as browsable folders so installers can access files without extraction steps.

state.title: Session Stability
state.desc: Maintains path state, cache and staging lifecycle to handle fragmented reads and repeated requests reliably.

footer.title: Built for practical install workflows
footer.desc: Designed to reduce manual prep, speed up transfer loops, and keep large archive sessions manageable on real hardware.

Puse.tagline: Frontend-first save editing for Pokemon Unbound
Puse.description: PUSE is a web-based save editor focused on fast local workflows: edit party, PC, bag and money data in-browser, recalculate checksums and export clean save files. Backend mode is also available for API-driven development.

local.title: Local Browser Mode
local.desc: Recommended runtime where parsing, editing, checksum and export happen entirely in the browser.

backend.title: FastAPI Backend Mode
backend.desc: Optional local API mode for debugging, development and workflows that benefit from Python tooling.

editor.title: Complete Save Editing
editor.desc: Edit party stats, moves and abilities, manage PC boxes, adjust bag pockets and tune money values in one interface.

runtime.title: Dual Runtime Strategy
runtime.desc: Switch between frontend-only and backend-powered execution without changing the product experience.

data.title: Rich Data Mapping
data.desc: Uses curated lookup tables and icon manifests to keep move, item and Pokemon references fast and consistent.

safety.title: Checksum-Safe Export
safety.desc: Recalculates save checksums before export to preserve compatibility and reduce corruption risk.

footer.title: Built for practical ROM-hack utility
footer.desc: A focused fan tool made to keep save editing simple, reversible and deployable as a static web app.
